title: Points of a site with finite limits are functors commuting with finite limits and coverings
author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: The proposition characterizes points of a site with finite limits as the functors to sets which commute with finite limits and turn coverings into surjections (statement lines 8525-8536). The proof is a complete argument in both directions: a point satisfies the second condition by definition and the first because the functor is the composite of three left exact functors (proof lines 8539-8551); conversely, a functor satisfying the two conditions satisfies the first two conditions of a point immediately, and its stalk functor is exact because it is a left adjoint commuting with finite limits by the companion result (proof lines 8554-8559). The non-formal content is the identification of the functor with a composite and the exactness input. The claim is H2: both directions written out with each input named.
